sections.history: Thiruparthanpalli is one of the 108 Divya Desams and belongs to Chola Nadu, in the village of Parthanpalli on the way from Sirkazhi to Thiruvenkadu. It is one of the eleven Vishnu shrines of Thirunangur, each sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. The presiding Lord is Thamaraiyal Kelvan Perumal, 'the consort of the lotus lady', while the festival image is Parthasarathy, the charioteer of Partha, that is Arjuna. Thamarai Nayagi, also called Sengamalavalli, is the Goddess. The Alvar's hymn places the shrine in the eighth century. Pilgrims of the Thirunangur circuit visit it on the road to Thiruvenkadu.
sections.architecture: The sanctum is crowned by the Narayana vimana. The temple tank is the Kadga Pushkarini, the 'sword tank', which takes its name from the legend told of this place. As across Thirunangur, it is a village shrine of the Dravidian tradition, modest in scale and close to its tank. Thamarai Nayagi, the Lotus Lady whose name the presiding Lord bears as his own, is worshipped as the Thayar, and Parthasarathy is the utsavar taken out in procession.
sections.legends: Tradition, as told from the Padma Purana, speaks of Arjuna on pilgrimage, grown thirsty, who asked the sage Agastya, then in penance here, for water. Agastya had none, and Krishna handed Arjuna a sword; with it he dug the earth and water gushed forth, said to be linked to the Ganga. Hence the Kadga Pushkarini and the name Parthan-palli, 'Partha's place'. Krishna is said to have shown himself here as Parthasarathy, and Varuna and the sages Agastya, Bharadvaja and Gautama are remembered as having done penance at this spot.
sections.festivals: The chief celebration is the Thirumangai Alvar Mangalasasana Utsavam in the Tamil month of Thai, when the Thirunangur Garuda Sevai is also held on the day after Thai Amavasai and the utsavars of the eleven shrines gather at Thirumanimadam. Parthasarathy's procession is a focus of the temple's calendar. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: A quiet village shrine on the road to Thiruvenkadu, where the pilgrim comes first for Thamaraiyal Kelvan and then for the tale of Arjuna's sword. Ask to see the Kadga Pushkarini and reflect on the water that tradition says rose from the earth. It combines easily with its neighbours among the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams in a single day's circuit.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Thai Garuda Sevai is the busiest day. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Parthanpalli lies about 8 km east of Sirkazhi in Mayiladuthurai district, on the road towards Thiruvenkadu. Sirkazhi has a railway station on the Chennai–Chidambaram–Mayiladuthurai line; the major airports are Tiruchirappalli and Chennai. Take a taxi or autorickshaw from Sirkazhi.
